model: Distributable Earnings capitalization at cost of equity (asset-manager GP; engine not used)

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: DE Shares Outstanding (Participating Common Shares 799.9M + Participating Partnership Units in Blackstone Holdings 443.9M), per 2Q'26 Share Summary. Blackstone Holdings units are economically identical to and convertible 1:1 into common stock, so DE-per-DE-share is the correct per-share intrinsic value for a common shareholder -- NOT the 752.6M common-shares-issued figure on the GAAP balance sheet, which would overstate per-share value by ~65% by excluding the ~40% of the economic interest held by Blackstone personnel/Holdings unitholders.
inputs.net_debt_note: Outstanding debt at par $13,192.7M vs cash $2,507M + corporate treasury/other investments $9,735M = net liquid corporate deficit of ~$951M ($0.76/DE-share). NOT added as a bridge item: DE is already post-financing-cost (Net Interest and Dividend Income/Loss is inside the DE bridge per Blackstone's own definition), so per the AFFO/distributable-earnings capitalization rule net debt is never subtracted a second time. The larger 'Cash and Net Investments of $22.7B / $18.23 per share' headline figure additionally includes GP/fund co-investments ($2.9B) and net accrued performance revenue ($7.5B) -- both are working capital that recycles into or converts into FUTURE realized DE, so folding them into a balance-sheet bridge on top of capitalizing the DE growth path would double-count. Net effect: no bridge adjustment, immaterial (-$0.76/share) if it were made.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable -- DE capitalization model; equity-based compensation is already deducted inside Fee Related Earnings/DE per Blackstone's non-GAAP definitions
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity via CAPM: risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST), beta ~1.35 (alternative asset managers carry above-market beta from operating leverage on performance-fee/realization cyclicality and AUM-market-value sensitivity; consistent with Analysis JSON's 'High' cyclicality rating for DE/GAAP net income), ERP ~5.0% => CoE ~10.95%, rounded to 11.0% base. Bull 10.0% (perpetual-capital mix reduces realization-cycle risk), bear 12.5% (realization slowdown + rate-sensitive real estate stress). No WACC/debt weighting used -- DE is a post-financing-cost equity flow, capitalized at cost of equity only, per the AFFO-style rule in dcf-methods/SKILL.md.
inputs.nci_treatment: Blackstone Holdings Partnership Units (the NCI in the corporate GAAP balance sheet) are treated as economically equivalent common claims and INCLUDED via the DE Shares Outstanding denominator, not excluded as a minority interest -- this is how Blackstone itself defines 'DE per Common Share' and is the basis dividends are calibrated to. Redeemable NCI in Consolidated (fund-level) Entities ($1.37B) is fund-level co-investor capital, already excluded from Segment DE/DE by construction (DE deconsolidates Blackstone Funds).
inputs.model_choice_rationale: Blackstone is a fee-driven alternative asset manager (GP), not a standard operating company: GAAP revenue and net income are dominated by unrealized mark-to-market performance allocations and investment income (revenue swung from -$3.1B in Q1 2020 to +$5.3B in Q1 2021 on the same underlying fee business) and are not decision-useful for a going-concern DCF. Owner-FCF is the wrong tool here -- 'free cash flow' as conventionally defined mixes consolidated Blackstone-Fund cash flows that belong to fund LPs, not shareholders. Blackstone's own management, sell-side analysts, and the dividend policy itself all use Distributable Earnings (DE) -- FRE plus realized net investment/performance income less realized taxes and TRA payments -- as the cash-available-for-dividends metric. This is structurally identical to the AFFO/distributable-profit capitalization the REIT and funds-manager rows of dcf-methods/SKILL.md route to: a post-tax, post-financing-cost, per-unit cash flow that should be capitalized at the cost of equity and never re-levered by subtracting net debt. Routed here by analogy to that row (GPT.AX/CHC.AX-style AFFO capitalization), since the routing table has no dedicated 'asset manager' row and no peer BX/APO/KKR/ARES DCF exists in this folder to follow. FRE (the recurring management-fee engine) is used as the growth-rate SANITY ANCHOR (it grows ~9-10%/yr, smooth) while DE (FRE + net realizations, i.e., the actual distributable/dividend-determining flow) is the flow actually projected and capitalized, since DE -- not FRE -- is what funds the dividend and represents total shareholder-available earnings.
inputs.notes: Fresh build, no prior DCF exists for BX. Historical annual DE: FY2022 $6,632.8M ($5.17/sh), FY2023 $5,061.0M ($3.95/sh) -- realization trough, FY2024 $5,966.7M ($4.64/sh), FY2025 $7,110.9M ($5.57/sh), LTM-2Q26 $7,876.6M ($6.15/sh). FRE (recurring management-fee earnings, smoother): FY2022 $4,412.6M, FY2023 $4,349.3M, FY2024 $5,282.1M, FY2025 $5,737.5M (+8.6% YoY), LTM-2Q26 $6,331.4M (+10.4% vs FY25). Base-case DE growth path decelerates from the current ~10-11% LTM pace to a 6% terminal rate, roughly bracketing management's guidance for 'a return to double-digit base management fee growth in 2027' plus continued net-realizations recovery, tempered for the historical volatility of the realizations component. DE Shares Outstanding assumed to grow 1.5%/yr (net partnership-unit issuance from compensation, partially offset by buybacks -- DE shares grew ~1.1% YoY 2Q25->2Q26).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: de_ltm_growth_yoy / fre_ltm_growth_yoy (converged ~10-11%), used as Year-1 base-case growth rate; DE's 3-year CAGR (2.35%) is materially depressed by the FY2023 realizations trough and is not representative of the current run-rate -- see growth_divergence_warning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: DE 3yr CAGR (2.35%) diverges sharply from DE LTM growth (10.8%) and from FRE's much smoother 3yr CAGR (9.15%). This is a realization-cycle timing effect, not a change in the underlying business: FY2023 was a cyclical trough for exits/realizations (Net Realizations fell 58% YoY per the FY2023 earnings release) that a short trailing CAGR window captures as a permanent slowdown. FRE, which excludes realization timing, is the more reliable trend indicator and supports the higher near-term growth assumption used in the base case.

base.narrative: DE growth decelerates from the current ~10-11% LTM run-rate to a 6% terminal rate as the realizations cycle normalizes and base management fees return to guided double-digit growth in 2027 before moderating. Cost of equity 11.0% reflects BX's high beta to capital-markets/realization cyclicality. Terminal growth 4.0% reflects continued secular AUM growth (institutional + private wealth + AI/data-center infrastructure) tempered to a sustainable long-run rate above GDP given still-low alternatives penetration.

bull.narrative: Private wealth/DC retirement channel and AI/data-center infrastructure financing accelerate fundraising and deployment beyond guidance; perpetual-capital mix (48% of fee-earning AUM, +15% YoY) keeps compounding, reducing realization-cycle risk and supporting a lower cost of equity (10.0%) and higher terminal growth (4.5%).

bear.narrative: Realization slowdown flagged for Q3 2026 persists longer than guided; higher-for-longer rates keep pressuring the still-meaningful real estate segment and BREIT/BCRED redemption sentiment weighs on private-wealth fundraising; competitive fee compression from Apollo/KKR/Ares/Brookfield/Blue Owl caps FRE margin expansion. Cost of equity rises to 12.5% on realization/cyclicality risk; terminal growth cut to 3.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: DE growth decelerates from the current ~10-11% pace to a 6% terminal rate as the realization cycle normalizes and management's guided return to double-digit base management fee growth in 2027 plays out, discounted at an 11.0% cost of equity reflecting BX's high beta to capital-markets and realization cyclicality.
scenario_narratives.bull: Private wealth, DC retirement, Credit & Insurance, and AI/data-center infrastructure financing drive sustained mid-teens DE growth; the growing perpetual-capital base (48% of fee-earning AUM) reduces cyclicality and supports a lower 10.0% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q3 2026 realizations slowdown persists, real estate and private-credit sentiment stay weak, and fee competition intensifies; DE growth stalls near mid-single digits and the cost of equity rises to 12.5% on elevated cyclicality risk.

entry_price.basis: Base-case DE growth path, discounted and terminal-valued at the 15% hurdle rate itself (not at cost of equity), per the entry-price-at-hurdle method.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Slightly higher bear weight than the house 15/50/35 default because DE/GAAP earnings cyclicality is explicitly flagged 'High' in the Analysis JSON, management itself guided to a near-term (Q3 2026) realizations deceleration, and the stock is already down ~12% YTD alongside peers on private-credit sentiment concerns -- the downside case is a plausible near-term path, not a tail scenario.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Blackstone is valued as an alternative-asset-management GP: Distributable Earnings (DE) -- the metric Blackstone itself defines as 'amounts available for dividends to Blackstone shareholders' and calibrates its dividend to -- is projected over 10 years and capitalized at the cost of equity, then divided by DE Shares Outstanding (which includes Blackstone Holdings Partnership Units held by firm personnel, economically identical to and convertible 1:1 into common stock). This mirrors the AFFO/distributable-profit-at-cost-of-equity approach used for REITs and funds managers elsewhere in this folder: DE is already a post-tax, post-financing-cost flow, so it is never re-levered by subtracting net debt. GAAP net income and conventional owner-FCF are not used as the primary metric because both are dominated by unrealized mark-to-market swings and consolidated Blackstone-Fund cash flows that belong to fund LPs, not shareholders.
key_risks_to_valuation: DE is inherently more cyclical than FRE -- a prolonged weak-realizations environment (repeat of FY2023) would push actual results toward or below the bear case

The DE Shares Outstanding denominator (1,243.8M) is ~65% larger than GAAP common shares issued (752.6M); using the wrong denominator would overstate per-share value substantially -- this is the single most consequential modeling choice in this valuation

No bridge was added for corporate cash/investments because the larger balance-sheet cash figures Blackstone highlights (GP co-investments, net accrued performance revenue) are working capital that will convert into future DE already captured by the growth path -- if that judgment is wrong and some of it is genuinely excess, this valuation is mildly conservative
Terminal value is 44-65% of equity value across scenarios, typical for a capitalization model but leaving results sensitive to the terminal growth/cost-of-equity spread

No dedicated 'asset manager' row exists in dcf-methods/SKILL.md and no peer (APO/KKR/ARES/CG/BAM) DCF exists in this folder for cross-check; the AFFO-capitalization analogy is a judgment call, not a prescribed route
